intro: Installing a wet room in Borthwickstreet comes with a specific set of challenges that you won't find in a standard plumbing handbook. This is a small, close-knit community in Midlothian where the housing stock ranges from solid stone-built cottages to newer modern estate homes, and each type demands a different approach when it comes to waterproofing and drainage. A wet room is one of the most significant bathroom upgrades you can make — done properly, it transforms daily life, adds real value to your property, and lasts for decades. Done poorly, it causes structural water damage that can be expensive to put right. Getting the right installer in Borthwickstreet from the start is genuinely important.
localContext: Borthwickstreet's older stone-built properties and period cottages present particular considerations for wet room installation. Stone walls, while incredibly durable, can be uneven and porous, meaning the tanking and waterproofing stage of any wet room project needs extra care and more thorough surface preparation than you'd find in a modern new-build. Floors in older properties are sometimes suspended timber rather than solid concrete, which affects how drainage is installed and may require additional structural work to create the necessary fall towards the drain. The modern estate homes in Borthwickstreet are generally more straightforward to work with, though they still require careful attention to waterproofing details. As a moderately hard water area, Borthwickstreet homes can experience limescale build-up on shower fittings and screens over time — something worth factoring into your choice of fixtures, with thermostatic valves and quality chrome fittings proving more resistant to the effects of hard water than budget alternatives.
serviceDetail: A professional wet room installation in Borthwickstreet typically follows a clear sequence of stages, and understanding what's involved helps you make informed decisions throughout. The process begins with a detailed site survey, during which your installer assesses the existing floor construction, checks for structural concerns in older stone properties, and confirms drainage routes. If you're in a period cottage with a suspended timber floor, this stage may reveal that a concrete screed or additional support is needed before waterproofing can begin — this is entirely normal and better identified early. Once the structural groundwork is confirmed, the existing bathroom is stripped out and the walls and floor are tanked using a specialist waterproof membrane system. This is the most critical stage of the entire project; the tanking must be seamless and correctly applied around every joint and corner. After tanking, the floor screed is laid to create the correct gradient towards the drain — usually around 1-2% fall — ensuring water flows away efficiently without pooling. Wall boards or tiles are then installed, followed by your chosen shower fixtures, screen (if required), and accessories. Throughout the project in Borthwickstreet, an experienced installer will keep disruption to a minimum, particularly important in a smaller community where tradespeople tend to take their local reputation seriously. The full process typically takes between five and ten working days depending on the scale of the project and the condition of the existing space.
pricing: Wet room installations in Borthwickstreet generally fall in the range of £6,000 to £12,000 for a complete project. At the lower end, you're looking at a straightforward installation in a modern estate home with a solid concrete floor and no structural complications. At the upper end, expect costs to reflect the additional work involved in older stone-built properties or period cottages — this might include floor reinforcement, extended tanking preparation, bespoke tiling to fit irregular walls, or upgrading waste and supply pipework. Fixtures make a significant difference too: mid-range thermostatic shower systems and quality tiles sit comfortably in the middle of the budget range, while premium fittings push costs toward the higher end. Always request a fixed-price quote that itemises labour and materials separately.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Borthwickstreet and the surrounding Midlothian area makes a genuine practical difference. A local installer will be familiar with the kind of stone construction common to older homes here, and won't be surprised by the quirks that come with period properties. They're also more likely to have established relationships with local building materials suppliers, which can keep costs reasonable and lead times short. Perhaps most importantly, a local tradesperson in a small community like Borthwickstreet has a strong professional incentive to do excellent work — their reputation travels fast, and most of their future work comes through word of mouth from the same streets and neighbourhoods.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built cottage in Borthwickstreet?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — but it requires more careful preparation than a modern home. The key steps are assessing the floor construction, ensuring solid structural support, and applying a thorough waterproofing tanking system to account for uneven or porous stone walls. An experienced installer familiar with older Midlothian properties will factor all of this into their survey and quote.

faqs.q: Will hard water in Borthwickstreet affect my wet room fittings?
faqs.a: Moderately hard water can cause limescale build-up on shower heads, valves, and chrome surfaces over time. Choosing quality thermostatic shower fittings and regularly descaling with appropriate products will extend their lifespan considerably. Some homeowners also opt to install an inline shower filter, which is a low-cost measure that noticeably reduces scale on fixtures.

faqs.q: How long does a wet room installation take in Borthwickstreet?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Borthwickstreet take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. Older stone properties or larger bathrooms can run toward the longer end of that range, particularly if additional floor preparation or structural work is needed. Your installer should give you a clear timeline at the quotation stage before any work begins.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Borthwickstreet?
faqs.a: In most cases, no. Wet room installation is considered permitted development and doesn't require planning permission. However, if your Borthwickstreet home is a listed building or sits within a conservation area, you should check with Midlothian Council before starting work. Building regulations may apply to drainage and ventilation changes, and a reputable installer will ensure compliance as part of the job.
